data.narrative:
Ares Industries is a Series A–stage defense and security company founded by Alex Tseng and Devan Plantamura that has raised $31M to date. Valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of 10 same-sector companies at Series A and Series B stages, including 8 private firms (Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, and others) and 2 public comparables (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS). The peer cohort spans valuations from $125M to $3.0B, with a median of $1.0B.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The peer-median approach, anchored to the 10-company sample, yields $1.0B. The stage-progression method uses the $31M raised as a proxy baseline, implying $70.5B in total enterprise value, then applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, producing $141.0B. The substantial divergence between these methods—reflecting methodological sensitivity to baseline assumptions—warrants conservative interpretation.

Synthesizing across both approaches yields a valuation range of $850M (low) to $162.2B (high), with a median of $71.0B. The peer-median figure of $1.0B aligns more closely with observable market precedent for frontier-defense companies at this stage and funding level. Key uncertainties include the stability of the defense-sector comp set, the appropriateness of stage-progression multipliers in an early-stage, high-risk context, and whether the $31M raised figure adequately captures the company's true capital needs or market positioning.
